summary: Updates BCP 101 to account for the new IETF Intellectual Property Trust. It is a Best Current Practice and updates RFC 4071. It was replaced by RFC 8714.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC updates BCP 101 to reflect the creation of the IETF Trust. It changes how some references to ISOC in RFC 4071 are interpreted for intellectual property matters.

questions: what did rfc 4371 change in bcp 101
subtitle: Updates BCP 101 to account for the IETF Trust holding and licensing IETF intellectual property.

tldr.problem: RFC 4071 assumed that ISOC would hold certain IETF-related intellectual property, but an IETF Trust had since been created.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4371 directs that specified ISOC references in RFC 4071 be read as referring to the IETF Trust for IPR matters and adds trustee duties.
tldr.outcome: This Best Current Practice updates RFC 4071 and was obsoleted by RFC 8714.

today: RFC 4371 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 4071 and was obsoleted by RFC 8714.

sections.title: Why BCP 101 Was Updated
sections.content:
The first version of BCP 101, RFC 4071, assumed the Internet Society would be the vehicle for certain IETF-related intellectual property rights. Since then, an IETF Trust had been created to hold that property.

The RFC says the update takes effect once approved by the IESG and the IETF Trust Agreement has been formally signed by its Settlors and initial Trustees.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 4071 named ISOC as the holder for some IETF intellectual property. This update reflects the creation of a separate IETF Trust.

sections.title: How the Trust Changes RFC 4071
sections.content:
The Trust was formed to acquire, hold, maintain and license certain property used in connection with IETF administration. Its Settlors contributed initial intellectual property; its Trustees are members of the IAOC, and the IETF as a whole is its Beneficiary.

For IPR administration under BCP 101, RFC 4371 says the IETF Trust, rather than ISOC, is the proper entity for ownership and licensing. It directs readers to interpret specified ISOC references in sections 3.1, 5.3 and 7 of RFC 4071 as references to the Trust, and adds trustee duties to section 3.2.
sections.plainLanguage: For the listed IPR matters, readers should treat references to ISOC in RFC 4071 as references to the IETF Trust. The update also adds trustee duties.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that it has no security implications for the Internet. Its subject is the entity that owns and licenses certain IETF intellectual property, not an Internet protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The document changes administrative references about ownership and licensing. It says it has no Internet security implications.

references.text: Austein, R. and B. Wijnen, "Structure of the IETF Administrative Support Activity (IASA)", BCP 101, RFC 4071, April 2005.
